result:
The proposed solution does not establish its answer, and I believe the answer is wrong.

- The solution rules out the octahedron with a vague claim: it says star-matchings leave some size-6 cuts without a matched pair. It gives no argument that covers every perfect matching of the 12 edges, so this is not a valid elimination.
- It then asserts, without proof, that the square antiprism has a pairing in which every edge cut contains a matched pair. It names no such pairing and checks no cuts, so this is unsupported.
- The closing appeal to "widely known literature" is not a justification.

I could not verify the exceptional graph by working through all cuts. From my recollection of the result on conflict-free cuts in planar 4-regular graphs, though, the single exception is the octahedron, which has 6 vertices. That contradicts the answer of 8.

VERDICT: REJECT
